prerequisites: The limit concept, the concept of continuity at a point and the derivative of a function

learning_outcomes.text: Solid theoretical and practical formation on the main concepts of differential and integral calculus of real functions of one real variable.
Theoretical and practical formation on differential and integral calculus of real functions of one real variable.
Approximation for real-valued functions using Taylor's polynomial and error evaluation.
Calculation of areas in cartesian and polar coordinates.
Application of differentiation and integral calculus of one real variable function.
Engineering problems of one real variable.
Practical formation on the main concepts and results of differential and integral calculus in R.
Knowledge of differential and integral calculus for one real variable functions.

syllabus_topics: Differential Calculus in R: Definition of derivatives, chain rule and derivative of inverse function
Polynomial approximations to functions: Taylor's polynomials and Taylor’s formula with remainder
Numerical series: properties, convergence criteria, alternating series
Reference of functional series and convergence interval
Integral Calculus in R: Riemann sums and the integral: Definition and properties
Primitive functions and integration by substitution and by parts
Areas of plane regions by integrals calculation
Volume calculations by the method of cross sections
teaching_methods: Theoretical-practical classes with presentations supported by slides
assessment_rules: The final grade (CF) is calculated as (T1 grade + T2 grade) / 2 if both T1 and T2 are 6 or higher, otherwise it is the grade of the Final Exam (EF) or the Examination of Resource (ER). To obtain frequency, students must comply with attendance regulations and complete at least one of the two written tests (T1 or T2) with a mark of 6 or more. Classification improvement is exclusively by written exam in future examination periods.
